extracted.intended_audience: senior/key personnel and other significant contributors preparing NIH grant biosketches for grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare NIH-format biographical sketches for senior/key personnel and other significant contributors, following the specified sections (Personal Statement; Positions and Honors; Contribution to Science; Research Support) and page/format constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall format and length
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the following information for the Senior/key personnel and other significant contributors. Follow this format for each person. DO NOT EXCEED FIVE PAGES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specified headings and ordering for each person; ensure the entire biosketch for each individual does not exceed five pages. Use the format consistently for all senior/key personnel and significant contributors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name field
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the person's full name exactly as it should appear on the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: eRA Commons user name
rubrics_metrics.description: eRA COMMONS USER NAME (credential, e.g., agency login):
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the individual's eRA Commons username/credential if available (example format: agency login).

rubrics_metrics.name: Position title
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the person's current position title (e.g., 'Professor of Medicine, Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine').

rubrics_metrics.name: Education/Training table
rubrics_metrics.description: EDUCATION/TRAINING (Begin with baccalaureate or other initial professional education, such as nursing, include postdoctoral training and residency training if applicable. Add/delete rows as necessary.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a table with columns: INSTITUTION AND LOCATION; DEGREE (if applicable); Completion Date MM/YYYY; FIELD OF STUDY. Begin with baccalaureate and include all relevant subsequent training (graduate, residency, postdoc). Add or remove rows as appropriate to reflect the individual's training history.

rubrics_metrics.name: A. Personal Statement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize the individual's qualifications, expertise, and relevance to the project; describe the role they will play on the proposed project and resources or access they will provide. Use this section to justify why the person is well suited for their proposed role. (Example in text: description of expertise, leadership roles, resources to be provided to the PI.)

rubrics_metrics.name: B. Positions and Honors
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List Positions and Employment (chronological employment history with dates), Other Experience and Professional Memberships, and Honors. Include relevant service on review panels, editorial boards, leadership roles, and awards. Provide dates and concise descriptions as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: C. Contribution to Science
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the individual's major contributions to science in narrative form (numbered or themed contributions). For each contribution provide a concise explanatory paragraph and list representative publications (lettered a., b., c., etc.). Where applicable, explain the significance, impact, methodological contributions, or policy relevance of the work. Provide a link to the complete list of published work (e.g., MyBibliography) if available.

rubrics_metrics.name: D. Research Support
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List ongoing and completed research support, including grant number, funding agency, role (e.g., Principal Investigator, Co-Investigator), project title, dates, and a brief description of the aims and the individual's role. Separate ongoing (active) support from completed support and include dates for each entry. Use this section to demonstrate current commitments and relevant past project experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide examples and citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Include representative citations under Contribution to Science and list of publications links (e.g., 'Complete List of Published Work in MyBibliography: [link]').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each contribution, include 2–4 representative, properly formatted citations (journal, year, volume/pages). When possible, provide a link to a complete bibliography or public author profile (e.g., Google Scholar, MyBibliography) to document full publication record.
